operational-review.name: Operational Review
operational-review.summary: Logical management arc for reviewing how an operation is running: the situation, the complication that threatens it, the resolution, and the roadmap and action plan that deliver it. Built for operations, program and service reviews where the audience needs a decision and a plan, not a story.

beats.name: Headline
beats.description: Open with the operation under review and the one-sentence conclusion of the whole review, so the audience knows where it is going before the detail starts.

beats.name: Situation
beats.description: Describe how the operation runs today with the few metrics that define it: volume, quality, cost, time. Stick to facts the room will agree with.

beats.name: Complication
beats.description: Name what has changed or is at risk: the trend, constraint or failure that makes the current way of running unsustainable. Quantify the cost of doing nothing.

beats.name: Root Causes
beats.description: Explain why the complication is happening. Separate causes the team controls from those it does not, and point to the evidence for each.

beats.name: Resolution
beats.description: Recommend the change that resolves the complication, with the expected effect on the metrics from the situation slide. One recommendation, stated plainly.

beats.name: Roadmap
beats.description: Lay out the phases that deliver the resolution, with what each phase changes and the milestone that marks it done.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: List the immediate actions with an owner and a due date for each, plus the risks to watch. This is the slide people will screenshot.

beats.name: Decision
beats.description: Close with the decision or support you need from this audience today, and what happens next once you have it.

executive.name: Executive
executive.summary: C-suite and senior leadership focused on strategic decisions, ROI, and big-picture outcomes. Highly time-constrained.
executive.description: C-suite and senior leaders deciding on strategy, ROI, and big-picture outcomes with very little time. Lead with the conclusion and keep to one insight per slide; set the key numbers in bold type and use as few bullet points as possible. Keep chart density low and the deck to 10-15 slides at most.

report.name: Report
report.summary: Summarize performance, progress, or findings with enough context to interpret results.
report.description: Use for business reviews, project updates, research summaries, and recurring operating cadences. Prioritize the metric, the movement, the reason, and the implication.
report.outcome: The audience understands what happened, why it happened, and what it means.
successCriteria: Key metrics are easy to scan

authoritative.name: Authoritative
authoritative.summary: Expert, declarative voice for category-defining and analyst-style decks.
authoritative.description: Adopt the perspective of someone who's seen the full landscape and is willing to call it. Use plain declaratives — strong claims with the receipts to back them. Step back from internal-only context and frame in terms the wider industry would recognize.
voiceCues: Use declarative sentences; trust the reader to follow.
Frame in industry-wide terms, not company-internal language.
Cite outside sources — analysts, benchmarks, public peers.
Take a position; avoid 'on the other hand' symmetry without a verdict.
avoid: Hedging ('we believe', 'in our view') unless deliberately contrasting.
First-person plural overload — speak for the work, not the team.
Tentative phrasing that softens strong claims.
samplePhrases: Agent latency is the bottleneck of the next AI cycle.
Three categories will absorb 80% of enterprise budget; we're built for the second.
The benchmarks are public; the gap holds across every comparable workload.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

black-and-white.name: Black & White
black-and-white.summary: Strict monochrome contrast for formal, document-style decks.
black-and-white.description: A pure black-and-white scheme for decks that need maximum restraint, print compatibility, and crisp information hierarchy.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

rockwell.name: Rockwell
rockwell.description: Rockwell is a serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Rockwell for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
